To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a user-friendly and efficient programming of industrial pick-andplace robots can be achieved with an intuitive human-machine-interface.

the presented approach for a humanmachine-interface allows operators without expert knowledge for programming to commission complex assembly tasks in a short time and that the time for commissionation can be shortened to less than one day.
the presented human-machine-interface allows the user to program the robot assistant in an efficient manner without any prior knowledge of robot programming.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a flexible human-robot system that can be used for industrial assembly tasks.
the development of a human-machine-interface for the commissioning of flexible robot assistants in industrial applications.
the question how the robot can be programmed in a way that the machine setters can commission the system themselves without expert knowledge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented human-machine-interface enables machine setters to easily and quickly commission industrial pick-and-place systems.
this human-machine-interface allows a fast and easy commissioning of flexible robot assistants for small lot sizes in assembly applications.
the human-machine interface is able to reduce the time for commission of a robot cell to a few hours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a user-friendly and efficient human-machine-interface for the commissioning of industrial pick-andplace applications with flexible robot assistants.
the presented approach enables the user to teach a complex assembly assistant in a few hours without expert knowledge.
we have developed a human-machine-interface for flexible pick-and-place robots that allows a user-friendly and fast commissioning of assembly applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to develop a human-machine-interface for robot assistants that allows machine setters with little programming experience to commission complex assembly tasks in a short time.

a shop floor based programming concept for flexible robot assistants can be successfully realized by intuitive operator guidance, specialized jog controls and a simple object selection and parameterization interface.
the proposed human-machine-interface is a valuable tool for the automation of assembly applications in industrial environments.
